t:
(a) In General.—Section 704 of title 18, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a), by striking “wears,”; and 
        (2) so that subsection (b) reads as follows:“(b) Fraudulent Representations About Receipt of Military Decorations or Medals.—Whoever, with intent to obtain money, property, or other tangible benefit, fraudulently holds oneself out to be a recipient of a decoration or medal described in subsection (c)(2) or (d) shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than one year, or both.”.  
    (b) Addition of Certain Other Medals.—Section 704(d) of title 18, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) by striking “If a decoration” and inserting the following:“(1) In general.—If a decoration”; 
        (2) by inserting “a combat badge,” after “1129 of title 10,”; and 
        (3) by adding at the end the following:“(2) Combat badge defined.—In this subsection, the term ‘combat badge’ means a Combat Infantryman’s Badge, Combat Action Badge, Combat Medical Badge, Combat Action Ribbon, or Combat Action Medal.”.  
    (c) Conforming Amendment.—Section 704 of title 18, United States Code, is amended in each of subsections (c)(1) and (d) by striking “or (b)”.

fable.w: This section amends a criminal statute (18 U.S.C. 704) to penalize fraudulent claims of receiving military decorations and to define "combat badge." It contains no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue over a federal decision. The only tempting reading is that it affects members of the public, but imposing criminal penalties on individuals is not involving outsiders in a federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section amends criminal statutes regarding the fraudulent receipt of military decorations. It defines crimes and penalties but does not establish any process for public participation, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The text is purely regulatory and punitive in nature.
qwen_block.s: Whoever, with intent to obtain money, property, or other tangible benefit, fraudulently holds oneself out to be a recipient of a decoration or medal described in subsection (c)(2) or (d) shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than one year, or both.

opus.w: This section only changes the criminal law on fraudulently claiming military medals and adds combat badges to the covered list. No outside party is consulted or involved before any federal decision. Courts and fines show up only as punishment for an offense, not as an outside party's right to challenge a government decision, so the procedural-looking reading fails.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting wrong reading:** Someone might read the criminal penalty ("fined under this title, imprisoned not more than one year") as involving courts and outside parties in a federal decision. That fails the definition. The section only amends the Stolen Valor provision of 18 U.S.C. § 704: it narrows what counts as an offense and adds combat badges to the list of covered medals. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body or consultation, and it does not give any outside party a right to sue over or object to a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a criminal statute to define 'combat badge' and prohibit fraudulent claims of receiving such medals. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in a federal decision-making process. The text is purely definitional and regulatory regarding criminal liability, with no mechanism for public input, advisory committees with outside members, or rights to sue.
qwen_chat.s: (b) Addition of Certain Other Medals.—Section 704(d) of title 18, United States Code, is amended— (1) by striking “If a decoration” and inserting the following:“(1) In general.—If a decoration”; (2) by inserting “a combat badge,” after “1129 of title 10,”; and (3) by adding at the end the following:“(2) Combat badge defined.—In this subsection, the term ‘combat badge’ means a Combat Infantryman’s Badge, Combat Action Badge, Combat Medical Badge, Combat Action Ribbon, or Combat Action Medal.”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the amendment to Section 704(d) involves "combat badges" which are awarded to military personnel, implying some form of recognition or participation. However, this section is purely definitional and criminalizing fraudulent claims; it does not establish a process for the public or outside entities to participate in federal decision-making. The text defines what constitutes a combat badge for the purpose of a criminal statute regarding fraudulent representations. There is no consultation, hearing, advisory board with outside members, or right to sue granted to non-federal parties. The actors involved are the federal government (defining the law) and potential violators (individuals making fraudulent claims). No outside party is involved in the *decision* of how the law is applied or defined in a participatory manner.
